tx-discrimination.title: Texas Business & Commerce Code Chapter 552, section 552.056
tx-discrimination.excerpt:
Sec.A552.056.AAUNLAWFUL             DISCRIMINATION.               (a)AAIn          this

section:


                                          4
               (1)AA"Financial institution" has the meaning assigned

by Section 201.101, Finance Code.

              (2)AA"Insurance entity" means:

                   (A)AAan      entity   described       by    Section       82.002(a),

Insurance Code;

                   (B)AAa fraternal benefit society regulated under

Chapter 885, Insurance Code; or

                   (C)AAthe developer of an artificial intelligence

system used by an entity described by Paragraph (A) or (B).

              (3)AA"Protected      class"    means       a     group    or       class   of

persons with a characteristic, quality, belief, or status protected

from discrimination by state or federal civil rights laws, and

includes   race,   color,   national      origin,       sex,    age,    religion,        or

disability.

      (b)AAA    person   may     not    develop    or    deploy        an    artificial

intelligence    system   with    the    intent    to    unlawfully      discriminate

against a protected class in violation of state or federal law.

      (c)AAFor purposes of this section, a disparate impact is not

sufficient by itself to demonstrate an intent to discriminate.

      (d)AAThis section does not apply to an insurance entity for

purposes of providing insurance services if the entity is subject

to applicable statutes regulating unfair discrimination, unfair

methods of competition, or unfair or deceptive acts or practices

related to the business of insurance.

      (e)AAA federally insured financial institution is considered

to be in compliance with this section if the institution complies

with all federal and state banking laws and regulations.

Added by Acts 2025, 89th Leg., R.S., Ch. 1174 (H.B. 149), Sec. 4,

eff. January 1, 2026.

tx-defenses.title: Texas Business & Commerce Code Chapter 552, section 552.105(e)-(f)
tx-defenses.excerpt:
(e)AAA defendant in an action under this section may not be


                                       8
 found liable if:

              (1)AAanother person uses the artificial intelligence

system affiliated with the defendant in a manner prohibited by this

chapter; or

              (2)AAthe     defendant      discovers      a    violation             of   this

chapter through:

                       (A)AAfeedback from a developer, deployer, or other

person who believes a violation has occurred;

                       (B)AAtesting,     including      adversarial           testing      or

red-team testing;

                       (C)AAfollowing guidelines set by applicable state

agencies; or

                       (D)AAif the defendant substantially complies with

the   most   recent     version    of   the   "Artificial      Intelligence              Risk

Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile"

published by the National Institute of Standards and Technology or

another nationally or internationally recognized risk management

framework for artificial intelligence systems, an internal review

process.

       (f)AAThe attorney general may not bring an action to collect

a   civil    penalty    under   this    section   against          a       person    for   an

artificial intelligence system that has not been deployed.

Added by Acts 2025, 89th Leg., R.S., Ch. 1174 (H.B. 149), Sec. 4,

eff. January 1, 2026.

tx-cure.title: Texas Business & Commerce Code Chapter 552, section 552.104
tx-cure.excerpt:
Sec.A552.104.AANOTICE       OF   VIOLATION;    OPPORTUNITY     TO   CURE.

(a)AAIf the attorney general determines that a person has violated

or is violating this chapter, the attorney general shall notify the

person in writing of the determination, identifying the specific

provisions of this chapter the attorney general alleges have been

or are being violated.

      (b)AAThe attorney general may not bring an action against the

person:

           (1)AAbefore the 60th day after the date the attorney

general provides the notice under Subsection (a); or

           (2)AAif, before the 60th day after the date the attorney

general provides the notice under Subsection (a), the person:


                                       7
                  (A)AAcures the identified violation; and

                 (B)AAprovides the attorney general with a written

statement that the person has:

                            (i)AAcured the alleged violation;

                            (ii)AAprovided supporting documentation to

show the manner in which the person cured the violation; and

                            (iii)AAmade     any    necessary       changes    to

internal policies to reasonably prevent further violation of this

chapter.

Added by Acts 2025, 89th Leg., R.S., Ch. 1174 (H.B. 149), Sec. 4,

eff. January 1, 2026.

moffatt-nature.title: Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024 BCCRT 149, paragraph 14
moffatt-nature.excerpt:
14. Mr. Moffat says while using Air Canada’s website, they interacted with a support
    chatbot. While Air Canada did not provide any information about the nature of its
    chatbot, generally speaking, a chatbot is an automated system that provides
    information to a person using a website in response to that person’s prompts and
    input. The parties implicitly agree that Mr. Moffatt was not chatting with an Air Canada
    employee.

cases.claim: The supplied section 552.056 prohibits intentional unlawful discrimination in developing or deploying an AI system.
Substantial compliance with the stated NIST profile or another nationally or internationally recognized AI risk framework qualifies the internal-review discovery route.
No other New York law imposes an AI disclosure duty.
The decision establishes that the chatbot had no escalation controls or technical guardrails.
The agency imposed a monetary penalty on January 10, 2026.
Avoiding the described action before day 60 requires an actual cure and the written statement with supporting documentation and necessary internal-policy changes.
Any NIST-compliant system is immune from all legal liability.
The decision was issued on February 14, 2024.
The attorney general can bring the described action 30 days after notice even if the person is still within the cure period.
NIST framework compliance is required for every discovery defense, including feedback and testing.
The latest supplied enacted version commences on July 1, 2026.
The supplied section 552.056 is a provision of the Texas Government Code.
The supplied header establishes that this proceeding was filed on February 14, 2024.
All activities of every insurance entity are exempt from section 552.056.
The supplied English rendering preserves the original German statement about what the court established.
Among the supplied versions, the enacted amendment replaces the earlier commencement date with January 1, 2027.
The original German says the court did not establish that the defendant used artificial intelligence.
The complaint requests a monetary penalty.
Section 1428 requires publication of the filed disclosure statements themselves.
Section 552.056 treats a federally insured financial institution as compliant if it complies with all federal and state banking laws and regulations.
Section 1428 distinguishes the 5 percent ownership reporting threshold for private or closely held entities from the 50 percent threshold for publicly traded entities.
The amendment states a January 1, 2027 effective date.
